doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: No return to normal; Butch's lung transplant and the new normal
summary: Butch says things will never go back to normal, having lived cautiously since his 2014 lung transplant.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well that’s a good attitude to have because yeah, change is constant, and especially now. There was an article in the last DownBeat, which I just read today, about how do you justify going to a music school now and spending the bucks and so forth when we have this situation. And they had a pretty good answer. They were saying a variation of what you did and people are going to be combining their musicianship with their technology innovations. And I think people have always had to figure out how to find a niche and I suppose that is true more now than ever.

I think so. And I think that’s exactly what they’re going to have to do. Because I have taken great offense at very nice folks who will say something like, “Boy I can’t wait until this is over and things get back to normal.” Things are never going to get back to normal. You know? So we have to figure out how we can operate in the new normal. I found that out, I’ve been living a new normal for over six years now. I had a lung transplant back in 19 — [20] 14. And I had to totally change my lifestyle around so wearing a mask, carrying, even in my office here, carrying hand sanitizer, I’m wearing gloves, I’ve got Lysol spray, I have Clorox wipes with me all the time. Over six years now, six and a half years. So this isn’t all that new to me. But it’s not going back to what it was. It never will.
So we have to figure out a way that we can survive and exist and create in the new normal. That’s all.
